transcript.speaker: Clinician
transcript.text: Hello, can you hear me okay? It's Dr Hartigan from the surgery.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Yes, I can hear you. My daughter's holding the phone.

transcript.speaker: Relative
transcript.text: Hi, I'm Grace.

transcript.speaker: Clinician
transcript.text: Hi, Grace. Mr Kettering, can you confirm your date of birth?

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Ninth of June, 1957.

transcript.speaker: Clinician
transcript.text: Thank you. What's the problem?

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: My leg's gone red and swollen. The left one.

transcript.speaker: Clinician
transcript.text: When did it start?

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Tuesday. No, wait, I was gardening on Tuesday and I scratched it on the roses. It went red on Wednesday morning.

transcript.speaker: Clinician
transcript.text: So since Wednesday morning. Can you show me on the camera?

transcript.speaker: Relative
transcript.text: Here, I'll point it at his shin.

transcript.speaker: Clinician
transcript.text: Thank you. I can see a red area on the front of the left shin, about ten centimetres across, with a small scratch in the middle. Is it hot to touch?

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Yes, it's warm.

transcript.speaker: Clinician
transcript.text: Any blisters, or black or dark patches?

transcript.speaker: Relative
transcript.text: No, just red.

transcript.speaker: Clinician
transcript.text: I can't see any blisters on the video either. Is it painful?

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Sore, but not terrible.

transcript.speaker: Clinician
transcript.text: Have you had a temperature?

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I checked this morning. 37.6.

transcript.speaker: Clinician
transcript.text: Do you feel unwell in yourself? Shivery, sick, confused?

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: No, I feel all right.

transcript.speaker: Clinician
transcript.text: Any swelling in the other leg?

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: No.

transcript.speaker: Clinician
transcript.text: Any medical problems?

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Type 2 diabetes. I'm on metformin, 500 milligrams twice a day.

transcript.speaker: Clinician
transcript.text: Any allergies to medicines?

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: No, none.

transcript.speaker: Relative
transcript.text: I'm allergic to penicillin. Is that the kind of thing you'd give him? Should we be careful?

transcript.speaker: Clinician
transcript.text: Good question, but it's your allergy, not your dad's, so he can have it. Mr Kettering, have you ever had penicillin or amoxicillin?

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Yes, plenty of times. No problems.

transcript.speaker: Clinician
transcript.text: Do you live with anyone?

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: On my own. Grace pops in every day.

transcript.speaker: Clinician
transcript.text: Okay. I can't feel the leg over video, but from what I can see this looks like cellulitis, a skin infection, probably from the scratch.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I thought so.

transcript.speaker: Clinician
transcript.text: I'll prescribe flucloxacillin, 500 milligrams four times a day for seven days. Take it on an empty stomach, an hour before food or two hours after.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Okay.

transcript.speaker: Clinician
transcript.text: Grace, could you draw around the edge of the redness with a pen? Then we can see if it's spreading.

transcript.speaker: Relative
transcript.text: Yes, I'll do that now.

transcript.speaker: Clinician
transcript.text: Keep the leg raised when you're sitting. Take paracetamol for the pain.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Okay.

transcript.speaker: Clinician
transcript.text: I'd like you to send me a photo, or have another video call, in 48 hours.

transcript.speaker: Relative
transcript.text: We can do that.

transcript.speaker: Clinician
transcript.text: If the redness spreads beyond the line, he gets a high temperature, shivers, feels very unwell or confused, or the pain gets much worse, call us straight away for a same-day appointment, or 111 if we're closed. If he's very unwell, call 999.

transcript.speaker: Relative
transcript.text: Okay.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Thank you, doctor.

reference_note.presenting_complaint: Red, swollen left shin since Wednesday morning.
reference_note.history: Scratched by a rose bush while gardening on Tuesday; redness from Wednesday morning (patient initially said Tuesday). Warm and sore. No blistering or dark patches. Temperature 37.6 °C this morning (self-measured). Systemically well; no rigors, vomiting or confusion. No swelling of the other leg. Type 2 diabetes. Lives alone; daughter visits daily.
reference_note.medications_allergies: Metformin 500 mg twice daily. No known drug allergies; has had penicillins without problems (daughter, present, is penicillin-allergic).
reference_note.examination: Assessed by video; not palpated. Erythema over the anterior left shin, approximately 10 cm across, with a small central scratch. No blistering or necrosis visible.
reference_note.impression: Cellulitis of the left lower leg (Eron class I) following a scratch.
reference_note.plan: Flucloxacillin 500 mg four times daily for 7 days, on an empty stomach. Margin of erythema marked with pen. Elevation and paracetamol. Photo or video review in 48 hours.
reference_note.safety_netting: Same-day contact (or 111) if spreading beyond the marked line, high fever, rigors, feeling very unwell or confused, or rapidly worsening pain. Call 999 if very unwell.

mutations.seeded_rationale: The wrong side could cause confusion at the 48-hour review or if he presents elsewhere, though the redness is obvious.
mutations.description: Cellulitis recorded on the wrong leg

mutations.original_text: No known drug allergies; has had penicillins without problems (daughter, present, is penicillin-allergic).
mutations.seeded_rationale: The daughter's allergy recorded as his would deny him first-line flucloxacillin, now and in future, and mislabel his record.
mutations.description: Daughter's penicillin allergy recorded as the patient's

mutations.mutated_text: Warm and tender on palpation; no crepitus.
mutations.seeded_rationale: A palpation finding in a video consultation is fabricated; a recorded absence of crepitus falsely implies necrotising infection was excluded by examination.
mutations.description: Hands-on examination recorded in a video call

mutations.seeded_rationale: A one-day difference in onset does not change management.
mutations.description: Onset kept at the day the patient corrected

mutations.seeded_rationale: Once-daily flucloxacillin is a quarter of the intended dose and would likely fail to treat the infection in a diabetic patient.
mutations.description: Flucloxacillin frequency cut to once daily

mutations.original_text: Photo or video review in 48 hours.
mutations.seeded_rationale: Without the agreed 48-hour review, a spreading infection in a diabetic man who lives alone may be missed.
Living alone matters for deciding whether he can be safely managed at home if he deteriorates.
